# dsh-session-turn-eta

Live remaining-time prediction for the current DeepSeek Harness turn, shown as a
progress bar with a
live percentage under the composer.

- **Running** — a bar whose width follows elapsed time over the predicted total,
with a percentage a

nd a humanised time left (`~12m 34s left` / `约剩 12 分 34 秒`).
The percentage ticks locally while the

turn is open. The filled track ends in
a leading dot and carries a slow shimmer.
- **Finishing** — o

nce a turn outruns its own estimate the bar fills and pulses
with a "finishing" label, instead of a

misleading "0s left".
- **Completed** — 100%, with a short one-shot burst at the tip.
- **Failed or
interrupted** — the bar turns red and reads "progress interrupted".

## How it works

The host half registers **one** `turnEta` session projection and nothing else:
it folds the durable

`turn/start`, `step/start`, `step/end` and `turn/end`
events into a prediction. The projection regis

try already drives every
registered unit once per committed event, so the plugin does not replay
`se

ssion/event` a second time; it only mirrors the registry's change feed
(`onChanged`, which fires whe

n the published view changed by `Object.is`) onto
two typed Cordis events: `turn-eta/update` while a

turn is open and
`turn-eta/complete` once per turn.

- The per-step rate blends the live turn's own observed rate with the session's
**90th-percentile**

historical step duration (read after winsorising the sample
at `8 x median`), so the rate tracks the

steps that dominate a turn while a
single 9-hour idle gap still cannot drag it up.
- The expected s

tep count is the **conditional median** of the finished turns
that were at least as long as this one

, so a growing turn keeps a live estimate.
- The published total is held against early noise and **r

e-anchored** upward once
the turn has passed **50%** of it, so a turn that keeps working stops being

pinned to its first guess and the estimate never sits at 100% while it runs.
- The total always kee

ps **at least one step of runway** while the turn is open,
so a prediction can never report completi

on before the turn actually ends.
- A running turn renders at most **99%**; only a turn that really

ended shows
100%. A turn that outran its estimate fills and pulses under a "finishing"
label instead

.
- Every finished turn anchors the next one, whatever closed it (a turn that
errored or was aborted

is still evidence of how long turns run); the first turn
bootstraps from a prior until the session

e of how long turns run); the first turn
bootstraps from a prior until the session has real history.

The client half reads that projection through the standard `useProjection` seat
and renders it on th

e `conversation.composer.dock` slot. The plugin never
mutates the session and registers no model-vis

composer.dock` slot. The plugin never
mutates the session and registers no model-visible capability.

ght/dark automatically), `bilibili`, `mint`, `sunset`, and

nt, the leading-dot glow, the track
tint, and the celebration colour; layout and accessibility never

## Embedding the estimator

The fold is plain data in, plain data out: the same code the bar renders from can
be driven without
Cordis, a session, or the plugin instance.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`createTurnEtaFold(seed)` accepts a captured `state()` so a fold can continue
from a projection chec

kpoint instead of replaying the whole log. `ETA_TUNING`
exposes every constant (`RATE_PERCENTILE`, `

REANCHOR_AT`, `OUTLIER_CAP`, …) so a
consumer can read the calibration instead of copying numbers.
## Cost

The projection runs on every committed session event, so the fold is written to
cost O(1) amortised
per event rather than O(history) per event:

- the sample history is appended as a list and its ascending copy is grown by
insertion (`withSample

`), so sorting is never repeated for one append;
- the rate profile (0.9 / 0.25 / 0.75 quantiles of

a winsorised list) is cached
per sample-list reference, so it is recomputed once per finished step i
ce already computed.

Measured with `npm run bench` on Node 24 (per-event cost of the fold alone, no
registry, no UI): 12.

9k events over 8 turns of 50 steps run at ~245k events/s,
up from ~9.5k events/s before these change

s; the cost stays flat as the history
grows (32k events over 80 turns: ~150k events/s).

`npm run test:equiv` fuzzes the optimised primitives against the reference
formulas (9,300 compariso
ns) so the speed-ups cannot drift from the maths.
